title: The Gingerbread Man
strapline: Run, run, as fast as you can — a chasing tale with a catchy refrain.
intent: A runaway story with a refrain every child can chant builds confidence with rhythm, rhyme and joining in.
Following the gingerbread man's journey — past the cow, the horse, the fox — sequences a story and maps a route.
Baking, chasing and the river-crossing give the tale endless play, from role-play to small-world to real cooking.
The sly fox raises gentle talk about trust, tricks and keeping ourselves safe.
The story invites real gingerbread cooking — measuring, mixing, waiting and change through heat.
implementation: Offer small-world figures — the little old woman and man, the animals, the fox, a river — and a gingerbread man to run the route.
Tell the story with a strong 'Run, run, as fast as you can!' so children are chanting it before you finish.
Follow the journey with the children: 'Who did he meet first? Who's next along the road?'
Set up a real bake as a linked provocation — mixing, cutting shapes, and the wonder of dough changing in the oven.
Bring in the safety talk lightly: 'The fox sounds friendly — do you think the gingerbread man should trust him?'
Let children choose the ending — caught by the fox, or a clever gingerbread man who gets away.
key_questions: Who did the gingerbread man meet along the way — can you remember the order?
How could he get across the river without the fox?
Can you chant the running rhyme with me?
Why did the fox pretend to be kind?
What happens to the dough when it goes in the oven?

impact.text: Children chant the refrain and retell the journey in sequence.
Children order the events and characters and recount who came next.
Children act out the chase and the river-crossing, inventing their own solutions.
Children talk about the fox's trick and what it means to keep safe.
Children bake gingerbread and notice the dough changing with heat.

enhancements: A gingerbread bake — cutter shapes, currant buttons, and the magic of watching them rise and colour.
A story map or road on the floor for running the gingerbread man past each character.
A blue-fabric river with the fox, for solving the crossing again and again.
Gingerbread-man decorating with buttons, icing and patterns to talk about.
Gingerbread-scented playdough with cutters for those who want to make, not eat.

playing_exploring: Children throw themselves into the chase and the chant, playing the story with their whole bodies.
They explore real dough — mixing, rolling, cutting — for the joy of it.
active_learning: Children work out how to get the gingerbread man across the river safely.
They see a real bake through from mixing to the finished, decorated biscuit.
creating_thinking: Children reason about the fox's trick and predict what he'll do.
They invent a new escape so the gingerbread man outwits the fox.
